The Green Fields Of Rossbeigh reel

There are 21 other names for this tune.

Also known as An Ciarraíocht, The Green Banks Of Rosbeigh, Green Fields Of Ros Beigh, The Green Fields Of Ros Beigh, The Green Fields Of Rosbeigh, Greenfields Of Rosbeigh, The Greenfields Of Rossbae, Greenfields Of Rossbeigh, The Greenfields Of Rossbeigh, Kerry, The Kerry , The Kerry Lasses, The Kerry Ring, The Kerry, The Kerryman, The Queen Of May, Shannon Shores, Tom Clark’s Fancy, Tom Clarke’s, Tom Clarke’s Fancy, The Witch Of The Glen.

Aka Tom Clarke’s Fancy

This tune was recorded as a set with “The Boys at the Lough” by Ed Reevy on the “Farewell to Ireland” boxed set and elsewhere in Reevy/Reevey/Reavy tune collections. On the “Farewell to Ireland” disc 3, track 10, the tune is the second one, though it’s listed fist.

Green Fields Of Rossbeigh

Kevin Keegan played Bdef afdB AFDF E2 etc. The high A is a unique touch, perhaps taken from Mike Hanafin’s 78, which is where the Green Fields title comes from. I hear Hanfin doing all kinds of things on his record and might transcribe it in full sometime. Here’s Keegan and Friends: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RLI_jlZsi_A

Josie McDermott’s album Darby’s Farewell

This is the first tune on track 1 of Josie Mcdermott’s album Darby’s Farewell yet on the album it’s called The Kerry Man. (More commonly known as The Lilting Fisherman.) If you listen to the track you can clearly tell that the tune Josie is playing is The Green Fields of Rossbeigh, not The Kerry Man (The Lilting Fisherman).

Re: The Green Fields Of Rossbeigh

Sorcha Costello plays Finbarr Dwyer’s version of the Greenfields of Rossbeigh three sets in (second of three reels) with accompaniment from Jakob Vester on this UCC Trad Soc recording:

https://www.facebook.com/ucctradsoc/videos/4320043291357806/

It’s quite different to the usual E Dorian setting of the tune and may be down a step in D Dorian. Does anyone know if this version is notated on this site? Perhaps under some other title?

↳ Posted by Alex Davidson on April 5th, 2021.

The Green Fields of Rossbeigh, Finbarr Dwyer

Hi everyone. I’d be grateful for any feedback on a Finbarr Dwyer version of this tune. Please see the full query from me at the bottom of the comments section here:

https://thesession.org/tunes/322#comment919058

Thank you, Alex

↳ Posted by Alex Davidson on April 6th, 2021.

Re: The Green Fields of Rossbeigh, Finbarr Dwyer

You’re probably better off asking Sorcha https://www.facebook.com/sorcha.costello.9, first of all where she learned it, she seems to have some doubt about the origins of the tune, so she probably picked it up on the fly from someone else who then said it was Finbarr’s version of the same tune, I’m not great on keys etc.. but I would go for A Dorian, the recording on Facebook is in Eflat, so you need to drop everything down a semi-tone, and it’s quite possible that Sorcha has changed the key down to Ador because the tune after is also quite a bit lower than the normal key.

↳ Posted by Theirlandais on April 6th, 2021.
